title: True Sea Moss: the next ad should begin with a *batch number*
dek: A recall changes the order of persuasion. Current operational proof has to answer the trust question before another benefit stack can matter.
lens: Functional food · trust repair · regulated claims
sources: True Sea Moss site + Whole Foods release + FDA recall record
footer_right: TRUE SEA MOSS · NOT CLIENT WORK

sections.heading: my strategic *read*
sections.body:
The public homepage leads with scale, ocean sourcing, daily ritual, and a wide benefit stack. A January 2026 FDA-posted recall involving all flavors and sizes manufactured before January 9 is also easy for a skeptical buyer to find. The FDA now marks that recall completed and terminated, but the current homepage does not visibly explain the operational change.

My read: the recall creates trust debt, and trust debt changes the order of persuasion. The buyer's first unresolved question becomes what changed, not what sea moss might do. More benefit copy would increase the burden of belief. The strongest future creative may therefore be an operational proof object rather than an ad claim. That direction remains blocked until current manufacturing evidence exists and is approved for use.

rows.claim: The recall is a verified public trust event.
rows.evidence: The FDA record says Diva Fam recalled all flavors, sizes, and batch numbers of True Sea Moss gel manufactured before January 9, 2026 because of missing regulatory authorization and temperature-monitoring records. The FDA page says the recall has been completed and terminated; no illnesses were reported in the announcement.

rows.claim: The brand subsequently announced a Whole Foods expansion.
rows.evidence: An April 22 release says three sea moss gels entered select Whole Foods stores and emphasizes transparent production and consciously sourced ingredients.

rows.claim: The current homepage spreads attention across scale, sourcing, ritual, and many benefits.
rows.evidence: The site cites customer and subscriber numbers, wildcrafted sourcing, energy, focus, digestion, immune support, metabolism, skin, hair, and daily minerals.

items.action: A · The batch is the ad · BLOCKED
items.why: Put a current batch number, date, and changed process on screen. Let operations carry the persuasion instead of asking a founder or creator to say trust us. This cannot be scripted from public information and becomes viable only after operations and counsel approve the evidence and exact language.

items.action: B · One spoon, one fruit-forward ritual
items.why: Demonstrate texture, serving behavior, refrigeration, and a single flavor in an ordinary routine. Keep the promise at product use and sensory experience. Do not stack immune, energy, gut, skin, hair, and metabolism claims into the same ad.

blocks.label: Concept A · operational proof · blocked
blocks.text:
A1  The next True Sea Moss ad should open on a batch number.

A2  After a recall, trust us is copy. Here is the current batch is proof.

A3  Put the jar, the date, and the changed process in one frame.

blocks.label: Concept B · taste and ritual
blocks.text:
B1  One spoonful people can picture beats seven benefits they have to believe.

B2  Start with the fruit, the texture, and the place it earns in the fridge.

B3  Before the benefit stack, make the ritual real.

sections.heading: where public evidence *stops*
sections.body:
No-launch hold: current manufacturing authorization, pH controls, temperature-monitoring procedures, batch traceability, testing records, recall-cohort exclusion, retailer status, approved response language, and claim substantiation remain unavailable in the reviewed public sources. A private operational repair may exist; this review cannot establish it.

No safety, purity, detox, disease, immune, microbiome, metabolic, or body-outcome claim should be drafted from this public research. Paid creative work cannot begin yet. The first engagement input is current-batch evidence plus operations and counsel approval.

ledger.used_for: Recall scope, reason, current terminated status
Current public positioning and benefit breadth
Post-recall retail trigger and public trust language
